intro_html: Keema matar is Pakistani and North Indian home cooking at its best: spiced ground beef simmered with browned onions, tomatoes, and sweet peas over rice. Each bowl carries 33 grams of protein for about $4.21 (at everyday cost). The spice rack does the expensive-tasting work for pennies.
cost_closing_html: About $4.21 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a curry an Indian takeout menu prices at $14 with rice. The whole spice lineup here costs next to nothing across the entire batch.
shop_smart: All seven spices together, cumin, coriander, chili powder, turmeric, garam masala and friends, cost about $1.09 this batch. Once the jars are on your shelf, that is 8 cents a bowl for restaurant flavor.
Seven onions browned slowly are the flavor base, and at $1.94 they are the cheapest depth money can buy. Do not rush that step.
Beef is two thirds of the bill at $21.60, so make this the week the 4 lb pack of 93/7 is on sale. Ground turkey also works when it is cheaper.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice: rinse, simmer covered with water until tender, and set aside.
Heat the vegetable oil in your biggest pot and cook the sliced onions until deeply golden, 12 to 15 minutes. This browning is where keema gets its flavor, so take your time.
Add the garlic, ginger, and minced jalapeno and cook 2 minutes, then stir in the cumin, coriander, chili powder, turmeric, and salt for 30 seconds.
Add the ground beef and break it up as it browns until no pink remains.
Stir in the diced tomatoes and Greek yogurt and simmer uncovered 15 minutes until the mixture thickens and the oil starts to separate at the edges.
Stir in the peas and garam masala, simmer 5 minutes, and season with black pepper.
Portion rice into 14 containers and top with an even share of the keema.
portion_html: Weigh the rice pot and the keema pot, subtract the empty pot number, and divide each by 14 so every box gets its share of both. Each bowl comes out to about 563 calories and 33 grams of protein.

steps: Cook the rice and set aside.
Brown the sliced onions slowly in oil, then add garlic, ginger, jalapeno, and the ground spices.
Brown the ground beef, then simmer with diced tomatoes and yogurt until thick.
Stir in peas and garam masala and simmer 5 minutes.
Portion rice into 14 containers and top with the keema.
